clue.text: One making mark with vice, but not on his cattle

definitions.text: One making mark with vice, but not on his cattle

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the two words are worked up into something new

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A rancher who brands things wickedly but leaves his own herd unmarked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges MARK and VICE. Samuel Maverick, a Texas rancher, left his calves unbranded, so an unbranded calf, and then any independent person, took his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Texan who left his herd unbranded gave his surname to strays and to independent nonconformists.

clue.text: African country has a rule in the motorway

indicators.note: in puts the article and the word for rule inside the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, London to Leeds
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: An African nation enforces a regulation on its motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in south-east Africa, formerly Nyasaland.

clue.text: "Stir the -s" .blood'; Bracing, brain' and sinew (Kingsley)

parts.note: a gap to fill from Charles Kingsley's Ode to the North-East Wind, about Norse sea-raiders

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse about a bracing wind with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley's poem praises the north-east wind that stirs the blood of the Norse seafarers. The clue as printed reads 'Stir the ---s' blood; Bracing brain and sinew'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse seafaring raiders of the eighth to eleventh centuries, whose blood the cold wind stirs.

clue.text: Flowing with honey, 'tis said, for the barons' victory here

parts.note: runny means flowing or liquid

indicators.note: 'tis said tells us to take the word by its sound

parts.note: mead is a drink made from fermented honey

explanation.surface: Honey that runs, mentioned in a history of the barons' triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAD sounds like MEDE. At Runnymede on the Thames in 1215 the barons forced King John to seal Magna Carta.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadow beside the Thames where King John sealed Magna Carta under baronial pressure.

clue.text: On the other hand, did .Mary show good judgment with her garden ?

definitions.text: did .Mary show good judgment with her garden ?
definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme's Mary is quite contrary, and showing good judgment is being wise

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme asks 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Means conversely; the second reading splits it as the rhyme's contrary Mary being wise.

clue.text: Get quickly to work after the bitterness

indicators.note: after places the piece for work behind the piece for bitterness

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone told to hurry up and get on with the job after a bitter quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at a horse's fastest pace, or any great speed, is to rush along.

clue.text: 11 was one shot from the saddle.

definitions.text: 11 was one shot from the saddle.

parts.words: 11 was one shot from the saddle.
parts.note: the 11-down shot was loosed by a mounted Parthian archer turning in the saddle

explanation.surface: A horseman's parting missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Parthian horse archers feigned retreat and fired backwards from the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parthian archer loosed a feathered missile from a bow while riding away.

clue.text: One ball the batsman can't stand up' to ?

definitions.text: One ball the batsman can't stand up' to

parts.words: One ball the batsman can't stand up' to
parts.note: a cricket delivery that spins, read as an injury that leaves someone unable to stand

explanation.surface: A cricket delivery too good for the man at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinning delivery from the leg side to the off is so called; read literally, a broken limb stops anyone standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery spun by the bowler's wrist to turn from leg to off.

clue.text: Unwanted guest.' could knock up a place

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, reads the word for knock from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rap is a knock
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher who might make a mess of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAP to PAR. 'Knock up' looks like a phrase; the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who lives off a host without giving anything back.

clue.text: Comparing say stonecrop ' with gin-rummy ?

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the word, not spell it

parts.note: read as a crop that grows on stones, a lichen

indicators.note: rummy means odd or strange, so the letters of gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a rock plant resembles a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: LICHEN is often pronounced like LIKEN. 'rummy' is split from 'gin' and turns GIN into ING. Stonecrop is properly a sedum; here it is read literally as what crops up on stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to compare, so likening is the act of drawing a comparison.

clue.text: President 'who went on the wagon

parts.note: not a teetotaller: a Boer head of state who as a boy trekked by ox-wagon in the Great Trek

explanation.surface: A head of state who gave up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' suggests abstinence from alcohol; read literally it is the ox-wagons of the Boer Great Trek, which Paul Kruger, later president of the Transvaal, joined as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Kruger, Transvaal head of state, travelled north with the Voortrekkers' ox-wagons in the 1830s.

clue.text: Noah's trap hit badly by, this

definitions.text: Noah's trap hit badly by, this

indicators.note: badly shows the letters of the three words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: Noah's carriage was damaged by something.
explanation.walkthrough: Parthian horse archers shot as they rode away, so a cutting remark made on departing is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounding remark delivered on leaving, after mounted archers who shot while retreating.

clue.text: The weather's fearful !

definitions.meaning: British slang for nervous or scared

explanation.definitionFit: Blustery conditions are gusty; in British slang a scared person is also called this.

clue.text: 'On the surface they're often diverting

definitions.text: On the surface they're often diverting

parts.words: On the surface they're often diverting
parts.note: not entertaining things: repairs to the road surface that send traffic on diversions

explanation.surface: Things that seem amusing at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverting' looks like 'amusing'; here it means sending traffic on a detour, and 'surface' is the tarmac.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to a highway's tarmac often force drivers onto detours.

clue.text: Follow suit, Frank!

definitions.meaning: in cards, to lead one red-suit card after another of the same suit
candid and intimate, as in a candid talk

explanation.definitionFit: Playing hearts on hearts follows suit; a candid personal conversation is also given this name.

clue.text: Heavenly bodies as a rule .

parts.note: not stars: the ranked orders of angels, and a system of rule by rank

explanation.surface: Stars and planets in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly bodies' suggests stars; it means the angelic orders, the celestial ranking of seraphim, cherubim and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranked order of authority, first used of the nine choirs of angels.

clue.text: Guilty man got the bird

parts.note: the condemned prisoner saw the judge don the black square of cloth, also the name of a warbler

explanation.surface: A convicted man was booed.
explanation.walkthrough: A British judge put on a black cap to pass a death sentence; it is also a songbird. 'Got the bird' looks like 'was jeered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey warbler with a dark crown, and the black cloth a judge wore to pass a death sentence.

clue.text: Those trying needlework

definitions.meaning: embroidered cloths showing stitches and lettering

explanation.definitionFit: Tasters test things; embroidered panels displaying a child's stitching skill share the name.

clue.text: Foremost author employed on newspaper

parts.note: the foremost one is the leader
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: The top novelist has taken a job at a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a newspaper's main editorial article, so the journalist who writes it has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who composes a newspaper's editorials, its leading articles, holds this post.

clue.text: Projection takes ages with this apparatus

parts.note: a cam is a projection on a rotating shaft
an era is an age or long period

explanation.surface: A film projector is slow to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' suggests films; it is the engineering cam.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for taking photographs or film, the apparatus of the scene.

clue.text: It goes for a pop-song in the nursery

definitions.text: It goes for a pop-song in the nursery

parts.words: It goes for a pop-song in the nursery
parts.note: the nursery rhyme line about which animal goes pop

explanation.surface: A children's tune that becomes a chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Pop goes the weasel'. 'Pop-song' looks like chart music.
explanation.definitionFit: The small mustelid in the rhyme that ends each verse with a pop.

clue.text: Study about a capital equine investment

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for study encloses the rest

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Research into an investment in horses based in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' here means clothing, as in vestments, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment in its old sense is clothing; a caparison is a horse's ornamental covering.

clue.text: Scope for cooking

definitions.meaning: a kitchen stove with hotplates and ovens

explanation.definitionFit: Means extent or reach, and a kitchen stove with ovens bears the same name.

clue.text: The moss variety is evidently no rolling stone

definitions.text: The moss variety is evidently no rolling stone

parts.words: The moss variety is evidently no rolling stone
parts.note: a rolling stone gathers no moss, so a stone with moss in it cannot be rolling

explanation.surface: A remark on a mossy stone that has stayed put.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss agate is a gemstone with green moss-like markings; the proverb says a rolling stone gathers no moss.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss agate is a semiprecious quartz with dendritic green inclusions resembling moss.

clue.text: Removes' stains from lances, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of lances might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone scrubbing the marks off knights' weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing or scrubbing gets rid of dirt and marks.

clue.text: Scrutineers at a stately home, do we hear?

indicators.note: asks whether what we hear matches, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Chequers is the country house of the British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Election officials visiting a grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEQUERS, a country house in Buckinghamshire used by the British Prime Minister, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutineers inspect and verify, so they are inspectors who verify.

clue.text: Flora has an 'outsize in 'pies

indicators.note: in puts the size abbreviation inside the word pies

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A woman called Flora is a large size in pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name; it means flowers, and posies are small bunches of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Posies are small bunches of flowers, and flora means plant life.

clue.text: Hold up price 'reductions, say, of ship's canvas.

parts.note: to stay is to support or prop up

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word by its sound

parts.note: a sale is a time of reduced prices

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper delaying discounts on sailcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like delaying; it means support, and a stay is a rope that supports a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular sail set on a stay, one of a vessel's sails.
